As somebody who has seen behind the curtain (to a degree) as well, I completely understand and agree with Jared's words. Star Citizen is incredible, ambitious, and unknown territory.

As a concierge backer, I get where everyone else is coming from.

The assets they're creating are incredible. I have no doubt the game will be finished to Chris' standards, eventually. They haven't exactly made a secret of the process being incredibly broken, unorganized, and wasteful as they try to establish (and re-establish) processes. But, when release comes, I think the wait will have been worth it. Despite my frustrations, I love the project.

If anything, this has demonstrated that a large-scale community with a significant investment into the creation of a game cannot handle the multi-year development cycle of a huge title.

That's why I have more faith in Star Citizen than many other projects, they fail to meet deadlines they set themselves and they explain to the community what they missed and why - communication goes a very long way, even with an army of users banging at the gates.

I was a pre-Alpha tester for DayZ, Steam moderator for the developers and also involved in moderating the bug tracker so I was very invested in the success of DayZ but they made (and continue to make) the same mistakes in failing to communicate properly with those that help them and the community at large.

They are treading new waters with SC and it's obvious to most people that there will be plenty of hiccups throughout development but I'm confident that they'll see it through to the quality that they want - most developers would have kicked Star Marine out the door in a barely working stage, I'm glad they are holding back with releasing it in a mess.

It's slightly frustrating that dates are pushed back but I'd rather they got it working right rather than pushing it out the door to appease the vocal minority.

In another thread about improving reading speed someone suggested to not to repeat words in your head. I was wondering if anyone has advice on how to do this? I try not to but if I don't read aloud in my head I can't seem to take anything in.

I did a speed reading course and was not told that, but rather to not say the words aloud. Speaking lowers how fast you can read because, well, you need to say the whole word before moving onto the next. Not repeating them in your head however seems to not make much sense, it is almost as you aren't reading what is on the page.
I think what OP means is that you are not supposed to read the words out loud in your head, like think every word you read like you would say it.
I find that viable, but to not take it in, at all, is rather difficult.
I think that when you do that, you don't retain as much information as you could. That's the thing with speed reading - your pace is faster, but you don't remember as much.

Here you go: http://www.spreeder.com/app.php?intro=1 . It gives you a certain amount of words (1 by default) at a time from a passage you select. You can change the speed if it's too fast or too slow.

I kinda have to whisper the words when I read. If I read out loud in my head, then i start daydreaming and my eyes keep reading but my brain takes a vacation. Not sure why this happens but its annoying to get through a paragraph and have NO idea what I just read.
For me it depends on the medium. I normally won't read the text of a novel aloud but I often find it useful when reading poetry. Otherwise I find I miss the meter or other wordplay.
I think you'll just break the habit if you keep reading. I used to be encumbered by the same habit, but as I got back into reading heavily, I started doing it a lot less and reading faster. GLHF
